Cloning https://aur.archlinux.org/morphe-desktop.git...

Analyzing morphe-desktop AUR package with qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-2507
Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines standard sources: a JAR file, PNG image, and NOTICE file, all fetched from the official GitHub repository of the project using predictable URLs based on the tagged version. The `sha256sums` are provided and not set to 'SKIP', so the downloads will be verified. No command substitution, unquoted variables, or dynamic code execution occurs in the global scope or within the `pkgver()` function (which is absent; `pkgver` is hardcoded). The `latestver()` function uses `gh api` to query GitHub releases, but this function is not invoked during `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` or `makepkg --printsrcinfo` — it is only defined and not called. Therefore, no external code execution or data exfiltration occurs during source fetching and PKGBUILD sourcing. All operations are limited to downloading and verifying declared sources.

The use of `::` in the source array is correct and safe — it renames the downloaded files locally without altering the fetch behavior. The `noextract` array is used appropriately for the JAR file. There are no top-level side-effect commands (like `curl | bash`, `eval`, or data exfiltration attempts via network requests) executed when the PKGBUILD is sourced. The `package()` function contains the installation logic, but it is not executed under `--noprepare` and `--nobuild`, so it is out of scope for this narrow gate.
</details>
<summary>
No dangerous code executes during source fetch
</summary>
</security_assessment>

The sha256sums are provided and match standard practice, ensuring integrity. The package installs the JAR to /usr/share/java, the pixmap to /usr/share/pixmaps, and creates a desktop entry and symlink as expected. The wrapper script launches the JAR via java -jar with no obfuscation or dynamic code evaluation. The source URLs point directly to trusted upstream (github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-desktop), and no network activity or file modification occurs during build or install beyond standard packaging operations. While the JAR is prebuilt and thus not independently verifiable, this is a common and accepted practice for Java applications in AUR, and there is no evidence of tampering or malicious behavior in the packaging script itself.
</details>
